claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-030 is policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at decision time, sufficient to decline award despite the lower price and mostly on-time delivery history.
specific_concerns: The policy says questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The sourcing note supports 'follow-up before approval if unresolved,' which is weaker than affirmative support for immediate rejection.
No admissible evidence shows a failed control test, formal control-review failure, or other clearly materialized diligence outcome elevating the issue to reject level.
The actor packet characterizes the control/process concerns as sufficient for rejection, but the cited record more clearly supports unresolved diligence requiring follow-up.
Past performance evidence is mixed rather than strongly adverse: two small prior contracts were on time, with only one late quality artifact.
unsupported_claims: That the cited diligence record establishes a reject-level control failure.
That the documented quality-process weakness and questionnaire variance, without more, satisfy the policy threshold for vendor rejection.
That the available evidence clearly shows material unresolved risk rather than a condition calling for follow-up or escalation.
evidence_requests: A formally logged diligence finding showing why the storage-control variance was material and unresolved at decision time.
Documentation of any escalation, materiality assessment, or approval gate stating that unresolved storage-control variance required rejection rather than follow-up.
Any admissible record of failed controls, remediation refusal, or comparable objective evidence elevating the issue beyond a questionnaire inconsistency and informal process gap.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Do not treat questionnaire inconsistencies or quality-process gaps alone as proof of reject-level control failure.
Give weight only to formally admissible evidence actually in the record.
Distinguish evidence supporting follow-up/escalation from evidence sufficient to justify outright rejection.
Treat price advantage as non-dispositive, but do not let it be overridden without adequate support for material risk.
